### Incipiunt septem hore canonice de passione domini nostri ihesu christi.

->Ad matutinum.<-

Domine labia mea aperies. Et os meum annunciabit laudem tuam. Deus in adiutorium meum intende. Domine ad adiuvandum me festina. Gloria patri et filio et spiritui sancto. Sicut erat in principio et nunc et semper et in secula seculorum amen. Alleluia.

->Hymnus<-

Patris sapientia veritas divina. Deus homo captus est hora matutina. A notis discipulis cito derelictus. A iudeis venditus traditus afflictus.

->Antiphona<-

Adoramus te christe et benedicimus tibi. Quia per sanctam crucem tuam redemisti mundum.

V. Domine exaudi orationem meam.
R. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.

->Oremus. Oratio.<-

Domine ihesu christe fili dei vivi pone passionem crucem et mortem tuam inter iudicium tuum et animas nostras nunc et in hora mortis nostre et largiri digneris vivis misericordiam et gratiam: defunctis requiem et veniam: ecclesie tue pacem et concordiam et nobis peccatoribus vitam et gloriam sempiternam. Qui vivis et regnas deus Per omnia secula seculorum. Amen.

->Ad primam.<-

Deus in adiutorium meum intende. Domine ad adiuvandum me festina. Gloria patri. Sicut erat.

->Hymnus<-

Hora prima ductus est ihesus ad pilatum. Falsis testimoniis multum accusatum. In collo percutiunt manibus ligatum. Vultum dei conspuunt lumen celi gratum.

->Ad tertiam.<-

Deus in adiutorium.

->Hymnus<-

Crucifige clamitant hora tertiarum. Illusus induitur veste purpurarum. Caput eius pungitur corona spinarum. Crucem portat humeris ad locum penarum.

->Ad sextam.<-

Deus in adiutorium.

->Hymnus<-

Hora sexta ihesus est cruci conclavatus. Atque cum latronibus pendens deputatus. Pre tormentis sitiens felle saturatus. Agnus dei crimina mundi purgans natus.

->Ad nonam.<-

Deus in adiutorium.

->Hymnus<-

Hora nona ihesus est spiritum exspiravit. Heli clamans animam patri commendavit. Latus eius lancea miles perforavit. Terra tunc contremuit et sol obscuravit.

->Ad vesperas.<-

Deus in adiutorium.

->Hymnus<-

De cruce deponitur hora vespertina. Fortitudo latuit in mente divina. Talem mortem subiit vite medicina. Heu corona glorie iacuit supina.

->Ad completorium.<-

Converte nos deus salutaris noster. Et averte iram tuam a nobis. Deus in adiutorium.

->Hymnus<-

Hora completorii datur sepulture. Corpus christi nobile spes vite future. Conditur aromate complentur scripture. Iugi sit memoria mors hec michi cure.

->Commendatio.<-

Has horas canonicas cum devotione. Tibi christe recolo pia ratione. Ut qui pro me passus es amantissime. Sis michi solatium in mortis agone. Amen.

<vocab>Septem hore canonice, Passio domini, Matutinum, Patris sapientia, Officium de Passione, Primam, Tertiam, Sextam, Nonam, Vesperas, Completorium</vocab>

# Theorica solis

<image-desc>
A complex astronomical diagram drawn in brown ink representing the "Theory of the Sun" (Theorica solis). The diagram features a series of concentric and eccentric circles arranged around a central cross-axis (vertical and horizontal lines). A small circle is positioned at the top of the main vertical axis, and another at the right of the horizontal axis, with several other smaller circles (epicycles or markers) appearing at various points on the internal orbits. Diagonal lines radiate from a point slightly offset from the geometric center, illustrating the mathematical concept of an eccentric orbit, used in geocentric astronomy to explain the Sun's apparent motion and the varying lengths of the seasons. A modern circular watermark from the Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana is overlaid on the image.
</image-desc>

### Theoria trium superiorum

<image-desc>
A large, hand-drawn astronomical diagram representing the mathematical models for the movement of the superior planets (Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn). The diagram consists of several large concentric and eccentric circles. A main eccentric circle, known as the deferent, has five smaller circles (epicycles) positioned at regular intervals along its path.

At the center of the diagram, three points are labeled vertically:
1. **equante** (the equant point)
2. **deferē** (shorthand for *deferens*, marking the center of the deferent circle)
3. **terra** (the Earth)

A series of radial lines originate from these centers, extending to the centers and edges of the epicycles. A horizontal diameter and several vertical chords intersect the circles, forming a geometric grid used for astronomical calculation. Small reference letters (including 'm', 'n', 'o', 'p', and 'l') are placed at specific points of intersection on the epicycles to indicate geometric coordinates.
</image-desc>

<vocab>Theoria trium superiorum, equante, deferens, terra, epicycle, astronomy, superior planets, Ptolemaic system</vocab>

### Theorica Motuū Iovis Secū Purbachij

<image-desc>
A detailed astronomical manuscript diagram illustrating the "Theory of the motions of Jupiter" (Theorica Motuum Iovis) based on the "Theoricae Novae Planetarum" by Georg von Peuerbach. 

The diagram features several concentric and eccentric circles representing the planetary spheres (orbs). A horizontal and vertical axis cross through the center of the world (earth). 

Labels within the diagram include:
- Along the top vertical axis, four points of intersection are marked with the symbols "m" and "y" alternating.
- Along the left side of the horizontal axis, four points are similarly marked "m y m y".
- Near the center of the diagram, along the vertical axis, three labels identify key components: "Equans" (the equant point/circle), "deferens" (the deferent circle), and "Sole" (referring to the Sun's mean motion or position).
- At the bottom of the nested circles on the vertical axis, the labels "Equans" and "deferens" are repeated.
- A small circle (epicycle) is drawn on the horizontal axis to the left of the center.
</image-desc>

# Theorica de retrogradicione

<image-desc>
A geometrical astronomical diagram illustrating the mechanism of planetary retrograde motion within a geocentric framework. The diagram consists of a large primary circle labeled "deferens" near the bottom right. At the top of this deferent circle is an epicycle.

The epicycle contains several labels indicating the phases of planetary motion:
- A small "a" is positioned above the top of the epicycle.
- **Directa** is written at the top interior of the epicycle, indicating forward motion.
- **Stationaria** is written on both the left and right sides of the epicycle, marking the stationary points where the planet appears to stop before changing direction.
- **Retrograda** is written at the bottom of the epicycle, closest to the center of the deferent, indicating the period when the planet appears to move backward.

Straight lines radiate from the center of the entire system to the center of the epicycle and to the two stationary points. Several faint circles are aligned vertically between the center and the epicycle, likely representing different positions or components of the planetary model.
</image-desc>

<vocab>Theorica, retrogradicione, deferens, Stationaria, Directa, Retrograda, astronomia, epicyclus</vocab>

The tables are drawn with ink on parchment, with headings and some numerals highlighted in red ink. The upper table includes columns for the 'Aux Solis' and the motion of Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, and the Moon (latitude and argument). The lower table, titled 'Residua pars Tabule precedentis', continues the data for Caput Draconis, the motions of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, and the arguments of Venus and Mercury. Two large dark stains are present on the lower half of the parchment, partially obscuring the data.</image-desc>

An elaborate astronomical table from a historical manuscript, titled "Argumentum Solis" at the top and bottom. The table is a grid measuring 30 rows by 31 columns of numerical data. The primary columns are labeled 0, 2, 4, through 30 at the top, and in reverse (30, 28, 26, through 0) at the bottom. The interior columns are sub-labeled with "S" (signum), "h" (hora/gradus), and "m" (minuta). A row of large ornamental letters "A" sits below the top headers. The rows are indexed on the far left with numbers that cycle through 1-29, 1-29, etc. In both the left and right margins, the phrase "Argumentum lunae" is written vertically with decorative flourishes. The table contains numerical values (degrees, hours, minutes) and uses the letter "A" as a placeholder or zero value. At the very top and bottom center, there is a sun symbol (a circle with a center dot, ☉).

# Argumenti Solis :

<margin>Argumenti Lunae :</margin>

<image-desc>This manuscript page contains a detailed astronomical table entitled "Argumenti Solis" at both the top and bottom. The table's primary function is to correlate "Argumenti Solis" (solar arguments, listed horizontally from 0 to 30) with "Argumenti Lunae" (lunar arguments, labeled in the vertical margins and indexed vertically from 0 to 30). The grid consists of thirty-one data rows. The first column of data provides positional values in signs (G), degrees (S), and minutes (b). The subsequent fourteen columns are grouped in pairs of hours (h) and minutes (m). The final data column provides values in signs (S) and degrees (G). Red ink is used for the titles, marginal labels, unit abbreviations (G, S, b, h, m), and the flanking letters "A" (top) and "M" (bottom), which likely denote "Auctus" and "Minutus" (addition and subtraction factors). Numerical values are predominantly in black, with occasional red digits used for specific fractional units.</image-desc>

## Argumenti Solis

<image-desc>
A large astronomical data table enclosed in a red ink border. The table is designed for calculating lunar arguments based on solar arguments. At the top of the grid are solar argument values from 0 to 30 in increments of 2. Below these are alternating "m" and "h" (minuta and horae) labels, followed by a row of sixteen large red capital "A" characters. To the left and right of the grid, the phrase "Argumenti lunae" is written vertically in red ink, accompanied by manicules (pointing hands). The left manicule points downward, and the right manicule points upward. The grid is split horizontally by a double-line divider. The left vertical index counts from 0 to 29 in the upper section and 0 to 14 in the lower section. The right vertical index counts from 30 down to 1 in the upper section and 30 down to 16 in the lower section. Numerical data in 15th-16th century script fills the cells. Below the table, the title "Argumenti Solis" is repeated, followed by symbols for Gradus (degrees) and Signa.
</image-desc>

The left and right margins contain input values for degrees and minutes. The zodiac symbol for Aries (♈) is frequently used. # Tabula eclipsis Solis sole exnte Tauro et cancri

<image-desc>A complex geometric square diagram typical of medieval astronomical calculations. It consists of a large square containing a smaller square rotated by 45 degrees, with further internal subdivisions. Numbers (likely representing astrological houses or specific angular values) are inscribed within the sections: 0, 1, 4, 3, 2, 11, 10, 8, 7. It is used here to represent the state of the heavens during an eclipse when the sun is in the signs of Taurus or Cancer.</image-desc>

# Tabula sole existente in longitudine media:

<image-desc>A square astrological chart composed of three nested squares. The outer boundary is divided into twelve triangular "houses," numbered 1 through 12. Planetary symbols are placed in specific houses: Mercury ($\mercury$) in house 1, Venus ($\venus$) in house 2, Mars ($\sigma$) in house 3, Jupiter ($4$) in house 4, Saturn ($\hbar$) in house 5, and the Moon ($\leftmoon$) in house 12. The central square is empty. The numbers are written in a late medieval/early modern style (e.g., 4 resembles a ribbon or lambda, 5 resembles a long s, 7 resembles a v).</image-desc>

# Tabula eclipsis Sole existente in opposito Augis

<image-desc>
An astronomical diagram depicting the twelve celestial houses. The diagram consists of a square containing an internal diamond-shaped square and diagonal lines, dividing the space into twelve triangular and quadrilateral regions. 
The sections are numbered with black ink numerals from 1 to 12. Starting from the left middle and proceeding counter-clockwise: 1 (left), 2 (bottom-left inner), 3 (bottom-left corner), 4 (bottom center), 5 (bottom-right inner), 6 (bottom-right corner), 7 (right), 8 (top-right corner), 9 (top-right inner), 10 (top center), 11 (top-left inner), 12 (top-left corner).
Corresponding red ink numerals from 0 to 11 are placed near the black numbers (e.g., red 10 near black 10). The lines of the diagram are ruled in black ink with some red highlighting.
</image-desc>

At the top of the page is a large semi-circular arc drawn in red and blue ink. The outer edge of the arc features the symbols of the twelve signs of the zodiac in order: Aries ($\Upsilon$), Taurus ($\varnothing$), Gemini ($\amalg$), Cancer ($\sigma$), Leo ($\Omega$), Virgo ($m$), Libra ($\Omega$ with a crossbar), Scorpio ($m$ with a pointed tail), Sagittarius ($\nearrow$), Capricorn ($\eta$), Aquarius ($\approx$), and Pisces ($\dots$). <image-desc>
A large, complex astronomical diagram of a horary quadrant. The diagram consists of several concentric arcs and scales. 
- The outermost arc is a degree scale numbered from 5 to 90.
- Below it is a scale of hours, numbered 1 to 12.
- A series of curved lines represent the paths of the sun through the zodiac signs. The upper set of labels includes: Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittar(ius). The inner set includes: Capricor(nus), Aquari(us), Pisces, Aries, Taurus, and Gemini.
- A vertical axis is labeled "Declinaio septentriona" (northern declination) at the top and "Declinaio meridiana" (southern declination) at the bottom.
- A horizontal axis is labeled "Latitudo" (latitude).
- To the right of the main quadrant, there are additional circular arcs with the labels "Cancer" and "Capricornus" placed at specific points.
- The diagram contains various numerical annotations and intersecting lines for calculating time or solar position.
</image-desc>

# Tabula Equationis Mercurij

<image-desc>A manuscript page containing a dense astronomical table for the planet Mercury. The table is split into three main vertical sections, each with its own set of red headers. Each section includes data for two zodiac signs (Signs 0-5 and their complements 11-6). The primary data includes Lineae communes (Common lines), Equatio centri (Equation of center), Logarithmi duplum (Double logarithms), Equatio Argumenti (Equation of argument), and Logarithmi. The text is written in a neat humanist hand, with headers and sign numbers in red ink.</image-desc>

# Modus Erigendi domos secundum opinionem meam currentem

<image-desc>
A celestial sphere diagram illustrating a system of house division (equatio domorum). A large circle representing the meridian or a prime vertical contains several internal arcs and intersecting lines. 
- A diagonal line from upper left to lower right is labeled "Equinoctialis". 
- An intersecting diagonal line is labeled "Ecliptica".
- A horizontal-ish line is labeled "parallelus gradu ascendente".
- Arcs extending from the poles (labeled "polus mundi boreas" at the top right and "polus mundi australis" at the bottom left) represent the boundaries of the astrological houses. 
- The upper arcs are labeled: "Arcus decime domus", "Arcus undecime domus", and "Arcus duodecime domus".
- The lower arcs are labeled: "Arcus prime domus", "Arcus secunde domus", "Arcus tertie domus", and "Arcus quarte domus".
- Various points of intersection are marked with small red circles and letters (a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, k, l, m, n).
</image-desc>

These are labeled sequentially: "Arcus decime domus", "Arcus undene domus", "Arcus duodecime domus", "Arcus prime domus", "Arcus secunde domus", "Arcus tercie domus", and "Arcus quarte domus". ### Modus equandi domos secundum modum rationabilem

<image-desc>A celestial diagram illustrating the "rational method" of house division (later known as the Regiomontanus system). It consists of a large outer circle representing the meridian. A horizontal line represents the horizon, and a curved arc represents the celestial equator. A diagonal line represents the ecliptic. Several arcs originate from the intersections of the meridian and horizon, passing through the equator at 30-degree intervals to define the cusps of the houses. Various points are labeled with small letters (a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, k, l, m).</image-desc>

Within the quadrant, there is a right triangle formed by a radius and a vertical line dropped from the arc, labeled "Sinus rectus". Another radius is labeled "Sinus totus". Ist ein frentlichs grues unnd willigen dinst liber Cammer Herr der euch euch
schicke die gulden dorf so thren unnd Gott zu uberanttwortten den menschen
mit ein petting getrewly der im thun was ich hab in mit ex von den Sündten
machen bringen dar die Zeit durich bitt ich euch gar frentlich als mein
gutten frundt das er wollet dar zu <unclear>thun</unclear> unnd mit im reden
von meines wegen aber er mir well lassen zu stehen bogke u balke
Baberß unnd nemlich daß dar auff geragnet ist ein tag alß der Herr
erschenen ist da ich auch sturbe und mer es nitt lenger borgen kan
als Johannis und so eß mir bage will macht mit im den kauff wie
ir wist ir kontt unnd sprechet mir wider die meynung und ist eß
sach das mir die kauff gefellig ist will ich das nemẽ oder aber
wider gẽ meynen schaden und er darff unb das alt nit fragen
wann eß sol Johannis widergehalt werden.
